complete_expression_findings.old_source: Pustet AP756 / printed[86], Orationes diversae 25 Ad repellendas malas cogitationes, Postcommunio, gives the complete petition with its actual Per Dominum cue. The whole petition is independently witnessed; an old partial Hadrianum similarity score is no longer the controlling whole-expression evidence.
complete_expression_findings.whole_petition_relation: The entire old petition agrees word for word with actual 1970 AP202 / printed209 after disclosed stress-accent removal, j/i normalization, joined wraps, ligature rendering and pointing. No additional petition fragment is borrowed from another prayer.
complete_expression_findings.appointment: 1970 AP201 / printed208 establishes Dominica IV in Quadragesima; AP202 gives Post communionem. The preceding Gospel conditions attach to the Communion antiphons and preface, not to this separately headed prayer. The opening rubric permits ritual alternatives for scrutinies; this candidate establishes the main formulary prayer and does not select an alternative or transfer its words.
complete_expression_findings.cue_preservation: The historical Per Dominum cue and the locally printed 1970 Per Christum cue remain distinct evidence. The former is retained in old-source apparatus; it is not silently expanded or swapped in a historical-human translation.
complete_expression_findings.ending_family: Fresh direct reading of 1970 IGMR32 AP31–32 / printed34–35 explicitly distinguishes long Collect endings from short offering/postcommunion endings and gives the Father-directed short branch. This prayer addresses Deus throughout; no Son is named at the end and it is not addressed to the Son. The local Per Christum cue selects that specific branch.
complete_expression_findings.formula_word_source: Pustet AP266 / printed180 independently gives the entire short formula Per Christum Dominum nostrum and separately labelled Amen. It supplies wording only, not this prayer’s appointment or family selection.
complete_expression_findings.response: Fresh direct reading of 1970 IGMR122 AP50 / printed53 specifically places the people’s Amen after the postcommunion prayer. This supplement avoids deriving postcommunion response placement solely from IGMR32’s Collect paragraph. The candidate keeps the response separate from the priest’s whole prayer body.
complete_expression_findings.secondary_control: Secondary digital 2002 AP150 agrees in the complete petition and short cue. That carrier does not authenticate a printed 2002 impression or 2008 wording.

english_fidelity.finding: Complete and faithful project study English, including the freshly proved short conclusion.
clauses: O God and everyone coming into this world preserve Deus and omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum.
Illuminate our hearts, we pray, with the splendor of your grace preserves the whole direct petition and quaesumus.
So that we may always think what is worthy and pleasing to your majesty retains both digna and placita, their dative relation to maiestati tuae, and semper.
And love you sincerely preserves te sincere diligere; the English modal may appropriately renders the petition’s valeamus.
Through Christ our Lord translates the separately established short formula. Amen remains a separate people response, not a silent addition to the priest’s scalar.
english_fidelity.authorship: New project study English, with no historical-human or approved-2011 claim.

finite_whole_expression_assessment.strongest_contrary_case: The complete body including this short ending is not the literal ending of the old Pustet prayer. Treating all prayer endings as interchangeable, extending a prior three-prayer method, or relying on an old prayer’s incipit would fabricate execution authority. A modern arrangement can carry new expression even when its pieces are ancient.
finite_whole_expression_assessment.assessment: The entire petition is independently old and unchanged; the entire short formula is independently old. A fresh same-edition local cue plus the specifically applicable short postcommunion rule establishes their finite 1970 execution relation, with a separate exact postcommunion rule establishing Amen placement. No novel petition wording or expressive recomposition is introduced by this conventional conclusion. This supports the bounded project-study projection while leaving the actual old ending and unresolved 2008 relationship visible.
finite_whole_expression_assessment.qualification_required: Complete 1970 source-local prayer, independently sourced from the whole 1862 petition and old short formula; new project study English; current 2008 target correspondence unresolved.
finite_whole_expression_assessment.prior_method_not_extended: No adoption of the prior three-offering-prayer short-conclusion passage or any Roman1962 execution method is implied; the new coordinate needs its own source and review records.
